Great game, with a very good and thought-provoking story and quite a lot of subversive storytelling as well. Ending E, the "true" ending so to speak, is just awesome in every way.
The gameplay is great. Hack and slash galore with dual weapons that can be upgraded during the game and quite a lot of side-quests for you to spend your time with. While thematically all the side-quests are pretty good, I'd say they are rather basic when it comes to in-game experience however: it's mostly just simple item fetching or enemy fighting, which never really gets old due to how well the game plays, but it does get repetitive especially near the end.
The story is pretty good, though I wish they'd focused and explored certain characters a bit more, somethings felt a bit a rushed here and there. All in all, fantastic ideas and a great exploration on what it means to be human and search for meaning. I just wish it would focus a bit more on its characters.
Also, the port is pretty crappy. I mean, you're basically forced to install the FAR mod for it to work properly and even then there are some performance issues. On my Geforce 1060, it wasn't really much of an issue, but those pesky pop-ups during overworld exploration and some noticeable frame-rate drops during exploration as well did annoy me through the whole thing. I guess it's Platinun's best port yet, but they certainly need to step-up their game from now on, least we always depend on some talented modder to fix fundamental problems everytime.
And with that, my message: "You must search for what it means to exist, despite that, there's nothing to worry about!"

*This will be a long review, somewhat personal, and may contain spoilers depending on how you interpret it.
In short, I think Nier: Automata is worth being the best game in 2017.
A general review with no spoilers of the story:
Pros:
+ 2B (this is probably personal)
+ Amazing amazing amazing sound tracks
+ Multiple endings with different playthroughs
+ Multiple characters to play with (2B, 9S, A2)
+ Upgradable weapons & Pods
+ A map that's not very huge, but contains a lot of fun discovering all its secrets
+ Customizable abilities for your character
+ Wide variety of combos produced by different weapons used together
+ Totally exceeded the price (judging by that I bought it during summer sales)
+ A very heart-touching ending in one of the endings
+ Deserves another plus for that ending
+ And another
Neutral (some players like it, some don't):
# Somewhat unexpected yet kind of expected story lines. Interesting story nonetheless
# Plot related side quests that contans lores and explainations for players who are interested in the background of the game and all that
# Combat system may be difficult for some players, but it is easy and fun for players that have experienced these types of games or with the help of some scripts (toggeling the Pod's fire button)
# Limited amount of weapons, but enough for your use judging by all the combos that diffrent weapons produced when combined together
# Some resources are hard to find/obtain (eg. Pure water), but you eventually get them without noticing as you progress through the game
# Has a mod that shows/reveals um..... parts of the body ( I think every game with a female character eventually get at least one of these mods :P )
# Texture mods and scripts are avaliable
Cons:
- 9S (This is personal as well)
- Sometimes the screen would go black for a second in cutscenes, doesn't affect gameplay though (no idea if it's the game or FAR mod or my computer's problem)
- Sudden quit during the credits in the E ending sometimes
- Do need some optimization on graphics and all that becuase it can overheat your graphic card if you turn on everything in the graphics catergory to the highest
- I guess that's all from me? Some players experienced other issues, such as crashing and all that, but I haven't encountered those issues, so no idea if it's the game's problem or if they need a better computer to fluently run the game.
Some pros below, cons are basically all listed and explained in the previous section, so yeah.
The Soundtracks are so beautifully intergrated. It fits perfectly with the game and the feelings that it wanted to express. Nier: Automata is the first game that made me cried. Not that I can't stop my tears, but I don't want to. A reason might be that I'm quite emotional and thus is easily touched, but not only me, many other players from around the world have had their eyes teared and cried out. There is this emotional power that laid within this game as you play to that part, the feeling of unity, of guilt, of sacifice, of hope and of blessings. It is so heart touching that for this one reason, it's worth to be the best game of 2017. These feelings that are hid within the game is what a good game should bring to us, but Nier: Automata is the first game that provided me with this missing part. Although there are some other games that can also provide feelings, such as online MMORPG games that you play with friends, but in those games, you might interact with online friends like how you'd interact with a friend in the real world. Nier: Automata is different. You don't know them, yet they did things that even friends might not have done for you. They deserve all the thanks and blessings that we can offer for them. However, even though there is this emotional power in the game, but if it wasn't for the soundtrack, this feeling wouldn't have been so strong and so touching. You can go search "Weight of the World" and listen to the song. It is by itself a good song, but when combined with the gameplay, it becomes epic; it suddenly feels alive. You can also go on forums to see how other players reacted to this soundtrack during the E ending, you can feel it even within their words.
Multiple endings and multiple characters gave more depth into this game and allows you to enjoy it more. The game is not over after the first time you finish it. It actually starts after you finished it for the third time, probably even the fifth time. If your game actually started at the sixth timeyou played it, you have my respect, and as well as respects and thanks from many other players internationally.
The hacking games and the time when you're on the flight unit is kind of fun. Very classical indeed, although some players might not enjoy them, but it did fit in with the game for some reason... Probably it's just my own opinions.
Despite some flaws, it is indeed a very good game.

GameLoading: Rise of the Indies was teased as spiritual successor to Indie Game: The Movie and could be watched as it.
It provides a deeper view on the indie dev community, especially the developer/community events and focus less on single developer / teams.
GameLoading: Rise of the Indies tells the stories of several indie devs and their latest games. They talk about their thoughts and feelings, being able to create their visions and pices of art. But also their worries and anxiety of failure, and that the final product is a failure or unnoticed.
This movie also encourages kids and young adults to dive deeper in the game development scene, as creational tools become more and more available.
If you are a fan of indies, are into the indie scene or just curious to find out if game development is your thing, this movie is a must-see!

Anyone who says this game is anything like Portal or Portal 2 has never even once seen any other first-person puzzle game in their entire life. Polarity is reasonably fun to play, you will constantly think you need the cubes and end up with one or two at the elevator and then later you will find out you're trying too hard on something that's easy if you bring another cube. All and all it's nothing too hard, nor too easy. Anyone who has played a couple of first person puzzlers will be able to solve this game, and for 0,19 euros it's worth for killing a couple of hours.

Equal parts Blacklight: Retribution and Monday Night Combat, Loadout manages to capture the charm of neither game and opts for an obscene, humorless aesthetic that simultaneously glorifies both early-onset diabetes and capitalist excess.
Weapon components can be unlocked through gameplay (via in-game currency), while cosmetic options (such as hair and clothing) can only be purchased using actual money.  It should be noted that while the developer took the laudatory step of including built-in colorblind settings, all players may find it necessary to take advantage of the alternate color options in order to differentiate between teams.  When the enemy names appear in red above their heads, but the opposing player is wearing green while fighting your comrades, whose names appear in green . . . good luck noticing that tiny red font amidst never-ending explosions, tracer rounds, and crimson laser beams (much of the level terrain is also red).
Those persons frustrated by incredibly fast-paced third person shooters with low-damage weapons (in which rocket-launcher wielding foes can bunny-hop with impunity) should definitely pass this one by.

This is without question an extraordinarily cute, fun puzzle game that just happens to be saturated in gore.
As a parody of 80's slasher flicks, Slayaway Camp succeeds and is also very addictive and fun. It never takes itself seriously and the result is an excellent puzzle game.
Its casual, its fun, its relaxed; the puzzles are interesting to work out and are generally in the 'sweet spot' of difficulty (i.e. they make you feel like you achieved something without being painful (and if any puzzle is painful there is a fair hint system and they'll even give you the solution if you need it)). The mood is very much a lighthearted dark-humor, and you can't help but smile when playing it.
Overall, this is a fantastic puzzle game; its funny, its cute, it delivers chuckles and intriguing puzzles. I unreservedly recommend it.

Stellaris is a game I bought on a whim because I need something to pass the time and has turned into probably one of the most engaging, enjoyable, and memorable games I have played; that I have over 400 hours at the time of writing and still find myself drawn to it should be a testament to that.
This continued enjoyment of mine come from the continued effort and care that the developers have put into this game; with all the patches they launch that add new content and fix the games features what didn’t work, and most of the problems I had with the game when I bought it have been addressed.
The only real problem I have with Stellaris is some of the late game gameplay.
In most all of my play throughs I usually end up controlling a large portion of the galaxy but am locked in an endless stale mate or cold war with other empires with neither side having the strength to attack the other and have a chance at winning, leading to huge spanses of time where nothing really happens.
The second problem I have is with the end game crisis, an extremely powerful late game event that threatens all empires in the galaxy. My problem with the end game crisis isn’t the crisis itself, (infact think it does help to break those endgame stalemates) but is with how AI empires try to deal with them, which is to say poorly. In most cases it tends to be the player vs the crisis, and if the crisis spawns near your empire and/or you don’t have a strong fleet to begin with it tends to be game over right there. Though if you are playing with other people you have a much greater chance to deal with it, as you can actively work with them and not just hope that the AI empires actually do something helpful.
Either way I still highly recommend Stellaris.

A sliding puzzle game centered around an 80s slasher/horror VHS franchise. The game tends to get harder as you progress but there's a learning curve to help.
You get coins in between rounds to put towards new kill-cams and towards hints or solutions for 25 and 100 gold each, respectively.
Each VHS tape has over 10+ stages, with usually a few 'deleted scenes' which are just alternate takes on one of the already existant stages.
You can unlock many different models for your killer.
My only real complaints would be that the loading screen mini-games where you get coins are simple and repetitive, needing some variety and better mechanics.
The different kills you can buy for 500 to 2500 coins each are cool, but over-time they tend to become just annoying. It'd be nice to see them change a little bit/have more then one method of killing per style.
I'd love to see some references/odes to films and franchises like 'Killer Klowns from Outerspace', 'Leperchaun', 'Jack Frost', 'The Gingerdead Man', and 'Puppet Master' among others in the future.
At first it seems boring, but the more you play the more you'll love it.

Why I originally bought it: Saw the Platinum stamp, was itching for a great action game and heard the story was amazing.
TLDR: Mediocre action game but the story was 'good enough' to get me to finish the game. I ended up satisfied albeit a little disappointed. Would recommend as this game will range from at least an okay game (wait for sale) or an amazing game (worth it at full price) if the story appeals to you. If you are unsure, definitely wait for a sale. I would NOT recommend this game on its moment-to-moment gameplay alone.
=================================================================
This is a highly story driven and thematic game. As such, depending on how well you connect with the characters and atmosphere will highly impact what you think of the game. For me personally, I had little connection with the characters but felt the story was 'good enough' to at least get me through the entire game.
Elephant in the room, yes the game runs poorly. System specs: i5 4690K, 8 GB RAM, GTX 970 SLI. Yes, I installed the FAR mod and you should too. I managed to get the game running at 1440p with everything on low. I frequently had ~10 fps drop in combat and every so often when walking around. Even running at 1080p, I frequently encountered similar stuttering and frame drops. Occasional game freezes coupled with no auto-save resulted in an hour or two of lost progress.
I felt the characters were too cold and devoid of emotion most of the time. As such, they were really hard to root for. Obviously they are androids so of course they are not supposed to have much emotion. Whether you like this type of character will ultimately determine how the story impacts you.
Standard post-apocalyptic style. Generally, I’m not a fan of this type of atmosphere and this game did not change my mind. I felt the grey undertones / relatively empty areas made the environment boring. After a while I just ran straight for the bosses as I had no desire to linger.
AMAZING! Obviously something that’s subjective, but I really enjoyed it!
Huge fan of Devil May Cry and Bayonetta. As such the combat was a letdown. The depth just isn't there. In general, all you do is mash light attack or heavy attack and dodge when necessary. I have also played a few bullet hell games and found the bullet hell sections to be trivially easy. Therefore, I found the moment-to-moment gameplay below average. I pushed through to finish the story. Cool idea to merge weapon based combat and bullet hell elements though.
As mentioned, I wasn’t a fan of the atmosphere so the side quests were not contextualized well for me. Most of the side quests are pretty standard fetch, kill, escort missions so I passed on most side quests unless I was in the area for the main quest. Some were good, but on average, I was not impressed.
A little weak on the customization. Character customization revolves around chip upgrades which are generally pure stat upgrades. Since you cannot string together weapon combos, I didn’t really feel the need to experiment with different weapons and all of them felt pretty similar. (Sure a light sword and a brawler weapon have different animations but they only differ gameplay wise in their dps.) As such I spent the entire game with my choice light weapon and my choice heavy weapon. Pod upgrades, the machine that shoots bullets from over your shoulder, do change the gameplay significantly.

I initially had mixed feeling about this. I mostly liked it but there's some small problems like how many of the bosses are disappointingly easy (possibly I should have played on Hard instead of Normal but that takes away the lock-on ability and I still did have some troubles in later areas). There's a fair few quests and side quests that feel a bit like boring busy-work too.
But despite the shortcomings I have to say overall I loved it. The story is really interesting and the gameplay is the standard Platinum goodness, with some interesting twists in gameplay like the mix of bullet-hell gameplay.
It's worth noting that if you get to the first "ending" (ending A) and just left the game there, you might come off feeling a bit disappointed. But as it turns out that's only half of the game. Play through again for the second ending and then the third playthrough is where it gets really interesting. I know that sounds ridiculous but give it a chance and you'll see.

Guns of Icarus is a fun, semi-fast paced teamwork based game set in a post-apocalyptic world where everyone flies steampunk airships and is fighting each other.  Don't let the teamwork word discourage you, though.  The community is wonderful, and the voice chat is actually very helpful, and helps a lot with group communication.  It's usually quiet, but if someone needs to say something relating to the game, they'll say it.  And, early in the game, they'll tell you how to get better instead of just getting mad you're not experienced.  The mechanics are great; all the components of the ship, hull, engines, balloon, and guns all have health and armor, and if the hull goes down and is destroyed your ships gets blown up.  Use the guns, which have four different stat bars so each is unique, to fire at and kill enemy ships, which are filled with real players so the game feels alive.  The community is a bit small, and going into matches does take a bit of time, but it's most certainly worth it for this amazing game.  With many character and ship costimization options, and a range of maps, Guns of Icars is DEFINETLY worth the $5 price tag.  If you are thinking about buying this game, BUY THIS GAME!  It's a load of fun, and with its fairly cheap price compared to many other steam games, I highly recommend purchasing Guns of Icarus.  (Also, Mac Support!)
Edit:  I'd like to note that you should not buy this game in its current form.  The vast majority of the playerbase has migrated to Alliance (myself included) and you should buy that instead.  Note the "Online" In the name.  The players for the online of this game have left, and so have I.  Don't buy this game.  Buy Alliance instead.  This will be 5 bucks you spent on a product which has been outdated and nobody uses anymore, which kind of makes it unplayable.  So yeah.  Buy Alliance, not Online.

Good concept. Decent puzzle design most of the time, but lots of occasions where it felt like the level designer ran out of ideas in the middle before they came up with enough puzzles to hide the goal points (like that one level where the third goal point was *in the room with the level exit*. Really?) Occasionally felt more like hide and seek than full on puzzling. Doing more clever things with the Polarity Switch mechanic would be good since it is the game's namesake. Lots of graphical mistakes - Getting your texture edges lined up with your geometry has been level design 101 stuff since the DOOM .wad days, gang. The game is low budget and it looks it.  Still, it kept my attention for the hour or so it took to play through to the end. 99 cents might be a good price point for this - I feel like I got my 19 cents worth out of it.

Great game! Easy to pick up and get absorbed by the story, i found myself repeatedly looking at the clock (1 am, 2 am, ...) and saying "just one more mission!"
I just love how everything is carefully crafted and well made: the story, the characters, the city, the pacing, the music, etc, everything's got a lot of "personality" to it... this may sound dumb but at times i really did feel part of the Saints, and came to really care for my allies and utterly despise the antagonists
Please note that you can't just go and play all the main storyline missions. You must perform certain activities to fill up your "respect" bar and only then you can move on with the story, but that's not as annoying as it sounds. Everytime i found myself with no "respect" left, i'd just go and clear a few activities... except demolition derby, racing (those are really tough), chop shop and hitman (too tedious) but there's plenty more that you can perform quickly and are actually quite fun (my favourites are septic avenger and trail blazing)
Just one more thing about activities: each one has several levels (not sure how many) but i found myself completing only up to level 3... after that they just got too difficult so i didn't even bother
There are a few missions (about 1/4) that are really "tight" (i.e. time limit is barely enough, or there's just too many enemies, or checkpoints are too spaced) and those i had to repeat up to 20 times -quite frustrating- but otherwise i cleared them the 1st or 2nd time so it's not that bad

I will start this review asking for every single one of you to take off your nostalgia glasses and judge this game for the year it was actually released.
While the original Skyrim in 2011 was a revolution, the same can't be said for it's 2016 counterpart that presented the same bugs and problem of the 2011 version, something that cannot be acceptable five years later just like outdated the combat system.
Bugs that I have to add were promised to be solved by Bethesda themselves back in the old Skyrim era, but such thing never happened and Bethesda never bothered to solve them.
The only difference bethween the 2011 ver and the 2016 is a 64 engine and improved grafics, that's all.
It's basicaly the same game of 2011 with slightly better grafics and a bit more of stability.
However you are paying 40$ for the same identical experience, when you could just buy the Legendary edition for a lot less.
In the end it's just the same juice in a flashy overpriced bottle, they didn't even bother making a better hud for PC users.
Oh and let's not forget Bethesda decided to hide the 2011 Skyrim in the store.
-
Now let's address the elephant in the room, Mods.
Mods have kept Skyrim alive and popular for years, however Bethesda was so grateful to all the people that kept their game alive that they blocked archivements for the mods users.
Sure, there is a mod to unlock them but that's not the point.
Sure, the choice was made to accomodate consoles but this is a PC, it's a different platform.
Bethesda is trying their best to monopolize mods, by inserting their own way to mod the game in the form of
, a site to which you have to sign in but be careful Bethesda simply didn't even care about fixing a bug that doesn't make you type in "@"
Now back on point, using
might be a good solution if you plan to have a little selection of mods but of course the right way to do it is by using the Nexus mod Manager.
Using such instrument is way easier then then you may think so just give it a try.
Now on the painfull note, Creation Club.
Many of you may think that the game shouldn't be judged for it, but the Creation Club is part of game it's not a different entity.
Let's see you have a game with many bugs you never bothered to solve, what you do? integrate a store inside it of course! what a brillant idea!
Praticaly the equivaled of adding another floor on an house with damaged pillars.
Also to add salt to the injury items from the Creation Club don't lock archivements despite such content being overpowered, for example an arrow that can one shot the Ebony Warrior.
In short everything it's legit if you pay.
Oh let's not forget that Creation Club's creators get paid only once then they lose every royalities to their own idea, while Bethesda keeps making money off of it and retrains every right.
Did you see a single author being credited on Creation Club? No? Good that's because they are not even credited for their own work.
Now I could spend hours talking about how Creation Club is an horrible system and a bad sign for future, but I will stop there cause I probably went a little off topic and I better stop myself now.
However I will leave you with a couple of questions.
Would you spend 5$ for a single armor set? or 4$ for a sword? Would you pay for a game mode?

doesn't have the same team oriented cohesive feel that RO2 had, feels more like a Battlefield game where you just run around and look for people to shoot and maybe cap an objective if it's convenient to you. Maybe it will progress over time. As of right now, there's only about 5 maps and like 3 of those are only available in "supremacy", AKA conquest mode from battlefield, which is boring and stupid. I miss the old days of RO2 where there was 2 defined lines of teams of 32 smashing into each other in epic coordinated battles.
Also, the mechanic where you can't use your gun in an objective an enemy has capped is really bad. You just run around with your gun down defenseless until you get to your friendly sector. Maybe this was implemented to prevent spawn camping, but it makes the game feel so constrictive in an already messy environment where people are already running around in random areas. It's like the developers *want* you to do that, but then you're forced to run back to your own lines when you lose a cap. Would be a very good game if these key elements were corrected.

Game was featured on my channel, now onto the review.
Short Review:
JOLT: Super Robot Racer is a quirky racing party game, its said a lot about these type of games but it is easy to learn and hard to master. While it is a fun "SpeedRunners" type game, at times it feels clunky which can be a good thing if you're not an avid gamer or it can throw you off if you're more experienced in the party racing genre. Simply put its a great game if you have guests over and want to play a game or two, but other than that it doesn't live up to what it could potentially be. I would love to have more fluid motion of characters, a menu after a game is finished instead of being sent to the main menu and perhaps an arrow pointing in the direction where we have to go (Although the confusion can be part of the fun).
For $5 I say go for it. Buy it if you're gonna have some friends over. But until the online feature is available, which will be coming soon, I say maybe hold off on it or get it on sale.

For the rest of you, lets get down to the nitty gritty.
What is stellaris? Well, think of civ but in space and without that weird art style. Actually, its more like total war but without armies. Eh, anyway. Resources go into creation and energy keeps creations going. Influence allows you to do political things like change policies, and unity helps you get new game changing mechanics.
The fluid and active interest you need to show in game is excellent. It is rare that you find yourself without a project to attempt to finish, or another power to talk with about trade or policy. The blended combat between fleets and invasion is well balanced and feels like it actually has weight. When you go to war over policy issues, mistrust, or border friction, you very well better be anchored properly with other factions. War can be costly, and you might lose planets. You might lose influence, or be destroyed, such as things go. Over all, you are always engaged and interested if you like scienceporn.
This game has one of the best soundtracks I've heard in many years. The responsive sounds used to indicate a selection add extra feedback to help immerse you. The OST is glorious and brings the game to life. The AI helper that assists you can be a little annoying to some people, but you can scrap it for parts, so there you go.
As the game is a Strategeeeeee game, graphical interests do not apply harshly, for this domain is mostly mental. The drawn art used to depict events is beautiful, and the aliens look realistic and believeable. Ships feel like ships, and the galaxy feels like a galaxy. You'd be hard pressed to find graphical issues here.
A nice blend of community feedback based DLC gives players excatly what they asked for, and a hell of alot more. Ringworlds, Dyson spheres, Space dragons. A little bit of everything. If you enjoy the game and want to throw money at getting new species or ships, they have that too. Don't forget that good old FREE dlc!
I'd say Stellaris is the top of a boiling lake of creativity. Older creations have led up to this monumental leap in Strategoooooo style gaming people look for. Community feedback is listened to even far after the game had its full release, and the staff is able to be communicated with personally if thats your bag. The science is spot on, and there is flavortext on everything you can possibly imagine. Alot of hard work and love was put into this game. If you remember anything about this review, remeber that the devlopers love their game for good reasons.

The game feels a lot like a student project more than a completed video game.
The story is almost non-existant, all you know is that you crash land on a planet and need to defeat some Russian named fellow.
The gameplay, while decent, feels very unoriginal. Sure the idea of a gun that teleports you to where it hits seems novel at first, but the game doesn't really do much to challenge the player with the ideas presented by the gun. Also, the only real areas that feel like you would benefit from understanding the game's mechanics are, oddly enough, the first few screens. You can shave off, roughly, 15 seconds there by using teleport and jumps and just knowing how the jumping as a whole works.
The absolute worst part of the game is the beginning and ending SHUMP sections though. The devs must not have known how to make a very good SHUMP because what they put forth was one of the worst I've ever experienced. The ship has can take several hits, which is nice because the hit detection can be a little wonky, but there's a lot of things that are just plain wrong. There's no invulnerablity at all after being hit in the ship, which means if you move incorrectly and get hit once you aren't given any time to regroup, you need to go into full panic mode. This also leads to another interesting glitch, which is also present in the normal sections of the game, if you get hit by something that explodes you take three hearts of damage. Be it a plane or missile in the SHUMP sections or the big monster's explosive shots. On the brightside, this allows you to finish the opening SHUMP section in 3 seconds as you only need to crash onto the planet and not beat the Russian guy.
The game is a good pickup if it's really cheap, because you won't be able to squeeze much more than 4 hours out of it, assuming you're attempting to 100% it, and those 4 hours will definitely not involve you being fully engrossed by the game.
If you want a Metroidvania game with more depth I recommend the Shantae games or Guacamelee.

Super House of Dead Ninjas combines fluid controls, retro gaming aesthetics with modern improvements, and lots of style without overdoing it, into a fun and fast paced platformer/time attack meets roguelike.
First and foremost the game handles like a sports car. I've played too many PC platformers as of late with slippery movement (I'm looking at you Spelunky) but it's very satisfying here. It really focuses on your reaction and skill which strives to make you improve. Very few deaths aren't your fault and the game rewards you for building upon your developing ability.
The pixel graphics aren't perfect but they aren't bad either. I do appreciate that while it has the retro angle going for it, it doesn't fall into the retro traps of being overly difficult or intentionally confusing. That said, later areas of the game can get *hard* depending on which mode you are on, but the learning curve is never unfair.
There are also a fair number of bonus features beyond the story mode. There are tons of unlockables, different weapons and spells, even costumes if you have the patience. I've also had a good bit of fun messing around in the level editor. While not terribly robust it shows how far you can truly push the game engine and your own abilities.
The game isn't perfect, there do tend to be glitchy parts (more than once I fell out of the side of the tower) but overall it is a well put together and fun package. You will probably get more playtime for your money here than many other games out there.

I love the King's Bounty games, I really do.
But King's Bounty: Legions just doesn't feel right. All of the elements that made the previous games interesting were removed or tweaked to provide the most bland and generic experience possible to the player.
In this game, there is no specialisation, you can spend your gold on marginal upgrades for units and spells, but cost scaling and level requirements for these upgrades is made in such a way that you can't just decide to dump all your gold into spells and rely on them. Especially since you can't learn spells, you have no mana, you have to buy scrolls, every time you use a spell you need to use a scroll.
When it comes to army building, there isn't much to it unless you are willing to pay, you have access to some basic units from shops, and a few advanced units as quest rewards, but only enough to show you what these units can do and encourage you to purchase more at the real money shop. You just don't get the satisfaction of doing your best with limited resources like you did in the previous games, especially since morale mechanics and most of the units special effects were removed.
Finally,  you don't have to select your battles like in the previous games, here you simply progress from one area to another with the ability to grind when you feel you aren't strong enough to take on the next challenge.
The only thing that's left from the previous games is the turn-based gameplay, which just isn't enough to hold the game together without the strategic elements that the previous games had.

Facebook adaptation of the Kings Bounty series. While they did an OK job and I guess existence of a facebook version of game can be justified as not everyone have PCs. But there is no reason to play a gimped up version riddled with mechanics that encourage microtransaction and other social gaming nonsense when you can play the real deal. You can get King's Bounty: Platinum Edition for 7.50$ on a sale and 1 dlc of this game costs more than that. Credit when it's due, this game does give you the option of PvP which you can't get from the others versions. If that's an important feature for you, you might tolerate the baggage it comes with but it's not worth for me.
RIP in peace King's Bounty, you will be missed.

A decent game by Hi-rez studios. It is very comparrable to Overwatch, however I haven't played Overwatch so I can't make any personal comparisons to it. What I can do however is give you my thoughts on Paladins.
Paladins has got mildly unique characters (about 30 different characters to choose from). There is enough variety and personality in the characters (especially with the in-game voices) that you will likely find one that you highly enjoy playing.
Paladins incorporates a simple voice command system (VGS) which allows users to easily communicate ideas and strategies even in the midst of gameplay without needing a mic. However, whilst the system is easy to use, it does take a fair bit of learning and study to effectively know the key-inputs for particular commands. It isn't something that comes easy to use for people unfamilar with the system.
Gameplay is decent. There are a variety of modes for things not to get too stale; classic point captures; payload pushes; and an incorporation of the two. The combat is fluid, responsive and not too overwhelming. Abilities feel good to land, and whilst the maps are large for a 5v5, Paladins adds mounts after dying to cover that distance better so you don't have to wander for 2 minutes to get back into the fray. The game has comeback mechanics, but not too much or too unfair. You are still at an advantage for playing better, but the game still gives the opposition a chance (in most cases) to win which typically makes every game exciting and heart-pounding til the end. The gameplay is fairly mildly paced, with games typically lastly around 15 minutes depending on the mode.
Paladins also includes cards that can be included into 'loadouts'. These cards give extra effects or bonuses to your abilities or character. This allows for a more personal gamestyle and more varied gameplay from game to game. Want to heal more? Want your abilities to knockback more or to not take as much damage (self) from your AOE weapon. This card system personally makes me love playing the characters so much more, they instinctively fit my style better and allow me to play in different ways.
The graphics are decent at best, they aren't great but aren't horrible unless you've got your settings at minimum. The art style is very particular, a bit on the cartoonish side. Isn't a whole lot to say about the graphics, really what you see is what you get.
There are several maps, different maps for each game-mode with several others still in development. They're large maps, and all vary greatly from one another, promoting different styles of gameplay and different tactics are required to play the different maps effectively. There are about 10 maps for the main gamemode 'Siege' and about 3-5 for the others, leaving good variety but still few enough to promote familiarty.
The store is fair, and mostly for cosmetics. I can't give you a whole of information on the store as I don't typically buy in-game currency or any optional extra in any game. However what I can say is the store is decently sized, with what seems to be consistant prices (in comparison to other games), although the UI for the store isn't great I have found and is a bit clunky to navigate.
Hi-rez studios are committed to creating a great game and their free-to-play buisness model is excellent. No need to purchase extras to compete with others. I respect them greatly for that. They generally respond in a reasonable amount of time to support tickets/complaints (personal experience), between 24-48 hours for the several times I've contacted them. Their passion for this game in undeniable and they are very friendly with the community. However this casuality with the community can be a bit rampant, and they lack professionalism at times when it is needed in the communication  department.
Overall, Paladins is a good quality game. It has some minor flaws, it does a lot of stuff well and 1-2 things really set it apart from other games like it. For a free-to-play game it is extremely good and you can enjoy many hours poured into it. I personally rate this game a 7.5/10.

For the rest of you, lets get down to the nitty gritty.
What is stellaris? Well, think of civ but in space and without that weird art style. Actually, its more like total war but without armies. Eh, anyway. Resources go into creation and energy keeps creations going. Influence allows you to do political things like change policies, and unity helps you get new game changing mechanics.
The fluid and active interest you need to show in game is excellent. It is rare that you find yourself without a project to attempt to finish, or another power to talk with about trade or policy. The blended combat between fleets and invasion is well balanced and feels like it actually has weight. When you go to war over policy issues, mistrust, or border friction, you very well better be anchored properly with other factions. War can be costly, and you might lose planets. You might lose influence, or be destroyed, such as things go. Over all, you are always engaged and interested if you like scienceporn.
This game has one of the best soundtracks I've heard in many years. The responsive sounds used to indicate a selection add extra feedback to help immerse you. The OST is glorious and brings the game to life. The AI helper that assists you can be a little annoying to some people, but you can scrap it for parts, so there you go.
As the game is a Strategeeeeee game, graphical interests do not apply harshly, for this domain is mostly mental. The drawn art used to depict events is beautiful, and the aliens look realistic and believeable. Ships feel like ships, and the galaxy feels like a galaxy. You'd be hard pressed to find graphical issues here.
A nice blend of community feedback based DLC gives players excatly what they asked for, and a hell of alot more. Ringworlds, Dyson spheres, Space dragons. A little bit of everything. If you enjoy the game and want to throw money at getting new species or ships, they have that too. Don't forget that good old FREE dlc!
I'd say Stellaris is the top of a boiling lake of creativity. Older creations have led up to this monumental leap in Strategoooooo style gaming people look for. Community feedback is listened to even far after the game had its full release, and the staff is able to be communicated with personally if thats your bag. The science is spot on, and there is flavortext on everything you can possibly imagine. Alot of hard work and love was put into this game. If you remember anything about this review, remeber that the devlopers love their game for good reasons.

Games that send up the slasher genre seem to have boomed in the last few years, with Until Dawn on the PS4 and Dead by Daylight on PC. Slayaway Camp takes that idea and applies it to a genre that seems ill-fitting at first: puzzles. But it actually works surprisingly well.
You play as the various different killers in the Slayaway Camp horror series, starting with a clear homage to Jason, and moving on to different antagonists in films that have increasingly less and less to actually do with summer camp. You slide them around the levels and guide them into their hapless victims, then watch the carnage. Sounds simple enough, but Slayaway Camp doesn't waste time introducing different puzzle elements. Your killer can move in any four directions until they hit a solid wall or victim, and naturally there are many times you need to make careful use of the terrain to get where you need to be. Sometimes even getting to the end of the level is part of the puzzle.
Complicating this is that even if they're stoned idiots, your victims are still smart enough to turn and run away if you move next to them, or kill someone they're adjacent to. Depending on the level, you might need to avoid this happening or exploit it. Early on the game also introduces cops, who will arrest you if you end up in front of them. I don't want to give too much away, as there are two shelves worth of movies and each one adds some new mechanic to worry about. It's very solid gameplay-wise, and there are plenty of 'aha!' moments to be had. The game's also pretty nice about hints, and you can pay a reasonable amount of the game's currency to get a solution to a level you're really stuck on.
So it's good that the game has substance and isn't just the aesthetic - but the aesthetic is pretty good itself. The normal animation for killing a victim is just the killer sort of jumping on them, but if you like you can use coins to buy special ones that can show up instead. These are exactly the kinds of silly deaths you'd expect from a self-aware slasher movie, and they're all fun to watch. My only complaint with them, and with the game at all really, is that getting the coins to buy them can be difficult. You receive them by beating a simple timing mini-game after each level, or doing a gauntlet of them you can access from the level menu, which goes until you miss. Getting all of them sounds like it could be pretty grindy, even with the cheesy 80s ballad that plays during the latter.
Aside from that minor quibble, I quite enjoyed what I've played of Slayaway Camp. It's an oddly addicting game, and I'd definitely recommend it if you're into the slasher genre or just puzzles. If you like both, you may have found your mecca.

A decent game by Hi-rez studios. It is very comparrable to Overwatch, however I haven't played Overwatch so I can't make any personal comparisons to it. What I can do however is give you my thoughts on Paladins.
Paladins has got mildly unique characters (about 30 different characters to choose from). There is enough variety and personality in the characters (especially with the in-game voices) that you will likely find one that you highly enjoy playing.
Paladins incorporates a simple voice command system (VGS) which allows users to easily communicate ideas and strategies even in the midst of gameplay without needing a mic. However, whilst the system is easy to use, it does take a fair bit of learning and study to effectively know the key-inputs for particular commands. It isn't something that comes easy to use for people unfamilar with the system.
Gameplay is decent. There are a variety of modes for things not to get too stale; classic point captures; payload pushes; and an incorporation of the two. The combat is fluid, responsive and not too overwhelming. Abilities feel good to land, and whilst the maps are large for a 5v5, Paladins adds mounts after dying to cover that distance better so you don't have to wander for 2 minutes to get back into the fray. The game has comeback mechanics, but not too much or too unfair. You are still at an advantage for playing better, but the game still gives the opposition a chance (in most cases) to win which typically makes every game exciting and heart-pounding til the end. The gameplay is fairly mildly paced, with games typically lastly around 15 minutes depending on the mode.
Paladins also includes cards that can be included into 'loadouts'. These cards give extra effects or bonuses to your abilities or character. This allows for a more personal gamestyle and more varied gameplay from game to game. Want to heal more? Want your abilities to knockback more or to not take as much damage (self) from your AOE weapon. This card system personally makes me love playing the characters so much more, they instinctively fit my style better and allow me to play in different ways.
The graphics are decent at best, they aren't great but aren't horrible unless you've got your settings at minimum. The art style is very particular, a bit on the cartoonish side. Isn't a whole lot to say about the graphics, really what you see is what you get.
There are several maps, different maps for each game-mode with several others still in development. They're large maps, and all vary greatly from one another, promoting different styles of gameplay and different tactics are required to play the different maps effectively. There are about 10 maps for the main gamemode 'Siege' and about 3-5 for the others, leaving good variety but still few enough to promote familiarty.
The store is fair, and mostly for cosmetics. I can't give you a whole of information on the store as I don't typically buy in-game currency or any optional extra in any game. However what I can say is the store is decently sized, with what seems to be consistant prices (in comparison to other games), although the UI for the store isn't great I have found and is a bit clunky to navigate.
Hi-rez studios are committed to creating a great game and their free-to-play buisness model is excellent. No need to purchase extras to compete with others. I respect them greatly for that. They generally respond in a reasonable amount of time to support tickets/complaints (personal experience), between 24-48 hours for the several times I've contacted them. Their passion for this game in undeniable and they are very friendly with the community. However this casuality with the community can be a bit rampant, and they lack professionalism at times when it is needed in the communication  department.
Overall, Paladins is a good quality game. It has some minor flaws, it does a lot of stuff well and 1-2 things really set it apart from other games like it. For a free-to-play game it is extremely good and you can enjoy many hours poured into it. I personally rate this game a 7.5/10.

Watered down, uninteresting version of King's Bounty: The Legend and its nice sequels. This started as Facebook game (which is where I tried it initially, long enough to see all the features) with microtransactions and a wait-or-pay-to-play system. Facebook login is not required to play unless you want any of the sharing features or cross-platform play with browser and mobile. Typical for this kind of game, you can expect constant "share this with your friends!" prompts and an unskippable mission to send gifts to friends, and so on.
The combat system isn't as interesting as the true King's Bounty games: gone are the three hero classes and the skill trees. No mana management, you have to purchase scrolls for each spellcasting. You don't lose troops, you just pay gold to resurrect them. Units can always move their full movement and attack or fire. Units are missing some interesting abilities they have in the "real" games. Side-note: animations are also inferior-looking and don't have the wacky character of the originals.
The overworld map shows its flash game origins and is a far cry from the gorgeous 3D maps of the original games. The quests are given in the usual dry facebook game style, and I haven't detected the trademark humor of KB:TL either.
Only redeeming factor would be maybe the presence of a PvP option, or the simple progression system which allows you to upgrade the stats of your units, as well as a simple crafting system.
Overall unless you're really interested in the social aspects or you're desperate to play this on your phone, I don't see a good reason why you'd play this instead of buying King's Bounty: The Legend. If you don't have it yet wait for the next bundle where you'll be able to get it for under 4$. (Google the "Wars of Ages" bundle for instance, should be up until mid-january 2013.)

Can you separate an artist from their work? Or in this case, separate a work from its publisher?
I’ll get this out of the way – the PC port is an absolute shambles. Resolution options don’t work (always displaying at 900p), the ambient occlusion interferes with AA options causing bizarre pop in, and the cutscenes are stuttering slideshows. That’s before we get to performance, which is abysmal for a game that visually would have been middle of the road a generation ago with stuttering, framedrops and random crashes.
The good news is that the FAR mod made by an enterprising modder goes a long way to sorting out a lot of these issues, with a big increase in performance and a fix to the resolution issues, though performance is still pretty dreadful for such a basic looking game. Square Enix, a multi million dollar corporation have done absolutely nothing, without a single patch since release and are content to charge £40 and leave a random dude to fix this broken mess.
I’d be tempted to leave a negative review because of this, but this leaves me in a bit of a pickle, as Nier Automata is one of the best games I have ever played. The original Nier was one of my favourite games of last gen, in spite of it at its core playing like a crap Zelda. Combat was clunky and weightless, it ran appallingly and the side quests were so awful I’m not sure whether they were a deliberate deconstruction of mindless gaming tickbox fetch quests. In other ways though Nier was incredible - the whole thing was bursting at the seams with imagination, both narratively and mechanically, managing to walk a fine line between dark humour and genuine, aching pathos.
Nier Automata manages to walk that same line, while having Platinum manage the mechanics and combat. Platinum are on fine form here, and fans of their other games will feel right at home – combat is slick, speedy and punchy and allows you to mix and match weaponry for a huge number of combos and fighting styles. You can also equip a certain number of upgrade chips, which while allowing you to further customise your experience also unfortunately allow you to break the game in two with a few regen/health steal upgrades.
In terms of openness, Nier shares more in common with old school 3D Zelda than more modern open world games – so yes, the desert is right next to the city which is right next to the forest (though we are spared the obligatory lava and ice worlds). While this can feel quite gamey, it has the plus side of making traversal speedy and easy. If I’m being honest there is still large areas of terrain without much going on, particularly in the desert – at it’s best this adds to the haunting feeling of isolation, but it just as often ends up just being tedious.
While the mechanics are perfectly serviceable, it’s the themes and narrative that make Nier the experience it is. It’s an incredibly sad game, an exploration into the cycle of futility and loneliness that comes from sapience. It delivers some of the most emotionally crushing gut punches I’ve ever experienced – it reminds me a lot of animated misery vehicle Neon Genesis Evangelion both in tone and content, with a thick layer of bleak nihilism almost, but not quite choking a thin but stubborn streak of idealism. Writing and acting is absolutely top notch in both languages, and while I would normally stick with the original Japanese, the quality of the localisation alongside the difficulty in reading subtitles during fast paced action sequences made English the preferred choice for me. Special mention should also go to the soundtrack, which is spectacular and honestly worthy of an entirely separate review.
It’s hard to describe why Nier:Automata is so affecting without wandering into spoiler territory – it’s such a dense game, with the multiple endings being absolutely essential to the experience. Like many people I got ending A and wasn’t sure exactly what all the fuss was about – sure it was fun, and dealt with some heavier themes than your average videogame but ultimately it felt very straightforward. The B and C route transform the game, and you realise how perfectly calibrated that first playthrough is to give the other routes maximum impact – previously seemingly innocuous exchanges are given heartbreaking gravity as the plot unfolds. It’s worth noting that these routes are NOT simply repeating the same content again – route B has some shared content from a new perspective, but route C is pretty much the other half of the game.
Even here Nier Automata isn’t perfect – sometimes it’s a little too on the nose (there is literally a robot called Jean Paul and features seemingly obligatory quotes by Nietzsche), and as much as I love android bums (and it’s a lot) I do feel the character designs are at odds with the serious narrative. For what it’s worth they do have an in universe explanation – but lets face it the real reason is that they wanted sexy android girls in gothic lolita dresses. A noble goal, but one that I think might turn away as many people as it brings in, and it would be a shame if anyone were to pass on this due to some over enthusiastic skirts.
This appropriately brings me full circle – can I really recommend the game in the broken state it shipped in? Normally I would say no just on principle, but Nier Automata is one of the few games worth gritting your teeth and abandoning your principles for – if just to support the funding of this kind of auteur production over the grey, designed by committee sludge that is typical AAA gaming.

This game had a great launch and was a ton of fun for a very short time. However, lax weapon balance and unsuited map design ended up completely killing it. People generally use nothing but Tesla weapons (Which make most guns nearly impossible to miss with), One hit kill / Remote Controlled launchers, or sniper rifles. You would think the game's fast pace and high speed movement would encourage close range combat, but more often than not, you'll be dashing across the map for minutes at a time to chase down the enemy team camped on a mountain in the corner of the map, spamming you with rockets and beams from a very safe distance.
The game's customization is nearly irrelevant at this point, due to a certain few weapon types being incredibly overused, with the rest being rendered hardly usable at all.
I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone at this point in time. The business model is horrible anyway. Predatory pricing runs rampant, with item prices placed slightly above premium currency denominations quite often, leaving you forced to buy more (or bigger) gold packs than you want to.
Avoid it like the plague. Unless this game sees a complete overhaul, it won't be on my list again anytime soon.

Your more than likely here because you love Red Orchestra 2 so I'll spare you the extra praise. This mod adds to that even more so. Great attention to detail and imo great map design for a free mod. This may very well be RO2's Darkest Hour if they keep it up. Now for my first true round in the full mod:
Joined a server that was just starting Omaha Beach. So for a fun time of dying I joined the Allies.  After spawning on the beach, I run to one of the
thinking that was going to be good cover, I mean it worked in MOHAA, it should surely work in this. Needless to say, the MG42 that was on the hieghts thought other wise. This led me to franticaly running between hedge hogs until decieding that a thick pole was good defensive structure on an open beach. This time the MG42 ripped me open. After a couple lives of dancing around the beach I finally get into a good crater and notice the MG42 in the bunker that was killing me. I line up the shoot with the trusty Garand and cleared the way for an advancing squad. After that I have a moment quite similar to this:
After a couple more Do-si-dos across the beach I get back to that spot and notice a squad of Germans taking shots from a far right sandbag emplacment on the hieghts. I again line up my shots and take out all 4 of them. After a while in cover we all moved up through smoke to the first bunker. Hiding behind that I took out some advancing Germans and a sneaky one hiding in a bush. As we move up the rubble the people next to me all get nailed by a MG42. So I run over and throw all 8 of thier grenades killing him. After some more deaths and skirmishes we move up to a house with a sniper killing everyone. As everyone likes to forget about bullets going thru things, I unload all 8 rounds into the wall into the area killing them. Now that we are advancing up a hill into the outskirts of a town another MG42 open ripping my squad to pieces. I drop prone and crawl up to his position, throwing a grenade at him and taking him out. I then sprinted to a stone wall that the enemies are hiding behind. After another MG42 opens up I pop over killing him and two enemies to then be instantly be sniped. After this I have a couple more lives taking a couple Germans with me. Next involved me running up the East edge of the ridge, not noticing my squad went a different route and ended up flanking about 8 Germans. After killing 3 with all 8 rounds, I notice a 4th bandaging. Instead of risking a reload, I charge with my bayonet, killing 3 more. I notice a MG42 team killing people trying to enter a small shed. I then charge in, stabbing another, then as I went to get the next guy running away, I run straight over an S-Mine causing my body parts to fly everywhere. That really startled me let me tell you. After a few more lives and kills we finnaly capture some sort of Hotel. After some more kills we advance to the next position. I notice fire coming out of a 2 story house. I proceed to toss in a grenade killing one, however as I went through the door a STG44 rips me a new one. After some more advanced I get back to the house and clear it out. After holding it for a couple minutes a 3 man team of Germans assualt. I kill one with my last 3 rounds in my M1. Then another takes a peak shot at me missing, causing me to pull out my 1911 and shoot at him 3 times missing. He then jumps through the window where I proceed to kill him with 5 more rounds. As Im about to start to reload another enters thru a window with a C96. I react pulling the trigger on the empty 1911 for a lovely click. He then shoots his last bullet at me missing. We then run at each other, with us both swinging our pistols like mad men until I finally hit him on the noggin, taking him out of the fight. Then a squad opens up, I get shoot a couple times to eventaully bleed out. Reminded me too much of this:
As we made a final push into the final objective, the game ended in us losing even though we were capturing the point. Although it may have said we lost, I felt it was a victory as in a real war we would not have a timer as we finally made it off the beach, and pushed them back, though at a great cost. I suppose, however, Omaha in 1944 was no picnic trip either. Thus ends my first round of many in this mod.
Cons: As much as this is great there are some minor things that came to mind for me anywhom:
-FPS suffered on Omaha in some spots (May be map optimization or my CPU crying)
-Needs more players ingame aka 128 instead of 64(yes this is a carpet complaint that extends to vanilla aswell)
-Omaha timer I feel should be a little longer, and perhaps more tickets for both teams(Round ended 40something US vs 0 Germans)
-Omaha should at least have a shingle wall at the end of the beach and a little more cover, maybe some extra craters or something of the sort (Unless I Missed a shingle wall that is)
All in all I was impressed by the mods fun additions to one of my all time favorite games. I highly suggest everyone who owns RO2/RS to get this well done mode. See you on the beach!

So with just over 900 hours invested in this game I think I can finally review the ol girl.
Well lets start with the pros..
1) Its in space, other than that Bones guy, we all love space.
2) The visuals, by Jesu the visuals are fantasitc, and plent of edits and extras in the workshop.
3) The Mods, seriously just have a look? Easiest way to see how many!
4) So many variations for species, traits, ethics, appearance, even more, once again, in the workshop... (have you looked yet?)
5) Its one of those games with a slow, normal, fast or fastest setting, so when you're chillaxing with your partner watching Netflix or whatever its not an issue, just pause the music (little player in the corner) and listen out for notifications, building complete, little dun duns when you're at your commerce cap, that sorta thing.
6) Despite what people say, it is very in depth, but some of the storylines take literally days worth of time for the investments to pay off, depending on the style of your galaxy, size, amounts of empires, crisis events on, it varies it greatly. It also takes some imagintion, aspirations, serious investment. All the diffferent play styles available and the mass amount of reading, worth it though and I'm bloomin aphantismic!
7) Crisis Events, just when you think you've mastered the game, this enemy ridiculously stronger than all of you comes out of nowhere, The Contingency wish to purge all organic life, The Unbidden, feed off it, and then theres others, if you left that setting on, just wait for the chaos. Everything will change, old enemies will become friends as you band together to fight your own wars another day. (or, if you're an asshat like me, you let your "friends" waste their fleets, deal with the enemy using that ridiculous fleet you just built, then proceed to conquer all. I never once said I ran a nice empire...)
8) Empires, Dictatorships, Monarchy, Democratic, all different types to play as, or just create your own random mix, run things the way you want to! (until some of your species modify themselves and think they're superior, build armies where they form, and its "F" to bring up search, helps when you have 80+ Planets in so many sectors, anyway they'll control or kill the asshats...)
9) The ships and stations, the weapon variations, subtle bonuses and big ones, harvested tech, oh and the DLC Utopia is a must, Megastructures really do change the pace of the game, you don't feel the need to scramble for planets, and in the late game you'll find habitats better than frontier outposts (little outposts that extend your influence, the colour on the map that corresponds to you)
10) The community, honestly the community for the game are great, plenty of guides and general advice, hell I guess even I'm contributing now? Also, the developers listen to the ideas of the community and are very responsive and friendly.
11) I think by now with the supplied screenshots, the gameplay videos available, community screenshots (check my own if you can? still not sure on all that jazz) you can make an informed decision to buy the game. Unfortunately, there are some negatives though, which I feel should be listed even with my all time favourite game!
Here they are then, those nasty cons!
1) The engine can get very slow late game depending on your processor, I found that an i7 6**** is best for the long haul big 1000 star galaxy games, but for 800 over lower an i5 4*** performs fine. When you see how much is going on in the game and all the calculations you understand its a downside that can't be avoided without massive changes, basically Stellaris 2 one day?
2) Diplomacy, its not atall terrible, but its also not atall great, it covers all necessity I guess? It would be nice to see more depth, and to have some more options to try and gain some frenemies. I hope that the devs are working on it because the Sythetic Dawn DLC really was just what the community asked for.
3) As brilliant as it is for Vanilla players, the constant updates can break a fair few mods quite often and it can take a while for the mod creators to update their files (completely understandable they're only human) always check the pages though as some are still compatible just stating they aren't. Comments from the community. Still when you're waiting six hours for an update you feel you can't play without, it sucks.
And thats my review, hope it was of some use to you! Goodbye, have a wonderful time!
Edit 982 Hours on record. Sod the new hate coming this games way, it isn't deserved atall, its whiney children having a rant about updates coming in the future, if you don't like them you will be able to roll back, stop the hate.

You work as a part of a crew on board victorian steam punk themed armed airship to complete objectives against other players attempting to do the same in their own ships. There just aren't that many games like it, and it does a very good job filling it's niche.
That being said, there are growing pains as one has to learn the strengths and weaknesses of ships and weapons, as well as learning how to play their class. After all it is a competitive teamwork game and all members of the crew have to perform in order to come out on top. The steam punk theme fits very well and the mechanics do a good job of making you feel like you're part of the crew of a steam driven airship.

A fun puzzle game with similar mechanics to
with a few notable differences in its gameplay. The most obvious of these differences is the way the player character is controlled. In
the player moves Agent 47 one tile at a time at their own discretion, whereas in
the killer is controlled like a rook in chess, moving in a single direction until they reach an obstacle or teenager unfortunate to be in their presence. The solutions to the levels are also more concrete than those found in
and typically don't offer room for variation in play style.
The puzzles are well designed and often difficult, especially later in the game. The game introduces new mechanics in each of the subsequent level sets, such as SWAT officers that can only be killed by turning off lights in the level, telephones that can be used to lure away certain targets from their positions and electric fences that can be used to kill teenagers without getting your own hands dirty.
The game also allows players to purchase (with in-game money) different killer characters and brutal ways of killing degenerate teenagers. The blocky, cartoony gore found in these unlockables is pretty amusing at first, but you'll probably find yourself skipping the short kill scenes after the first few times. The humor of the game is serviceable; if you're a fan of awful 90s slasher flicks then you'll definitely pick on some fun parodies of genre tropes.
Overall, a pretty good purchase if you're looking for a cheap time waster. Recommended.

Polarity is a first person logic puzzle game whose concept is vastly inspired by Portal. It has similar mechanics but at the same time it is full of originality. The companion cubes might not be as cute as in Portal, but they’re still present in this game and needed to complete the puzzles. An innovation consists in the ability of the player to switch between two polarities (red – blue) which allows him to run through gates or to jump on platforms, according to the selected polarity.
The single player part consists of 14 puzzles that are not too hard to solve, with difficulty increasing  each level though. However, even the most difficult levels can be solved in less than 5 minutes each. The 10 bonus levels are slightly more difficult to figure out, but they add new fun features to the game.
The coop mode, on the other hand, is quite challenging. The two players must cooperate to solve the puzzles that are much more complex than in single player mode. The levels are bigger, now consisting in multiple rooms. The path to the exit isn’t usually the same for the two players, but nevertheless, they need to work together to reach it. There are places in which timed jumps are needed while trying to grab certain objects at the same time, and these jumps are not easily performed with a controller as compared to a mouse and keyboard setup. Sadly, the game offers only local coop and not online multiplayer, so make sure to invite a friend that can be persuaded to work on those together with you, without him losing his patience. Or even better, maybe you can convince him/her to do those tricky jumps :)
Don’t hesitate to buy it, especially discounted, since it is a very fun game!

I picked this up because it looked good and the price was right. Had a technical issue with the mouse not responding. The tech support at Flying Tiger were on it and the issue was resoled in less than 24 hours. Great support and customer service.
Ive played through the Training tutotial and two of the missions while live streaming the gameplay @ 720P (the game's highest resolution) run at full screen on a true 1080P monitor. Ran very smoothly with zero glitching, lagging nor frame drops, even with alot of fire or action on screen.
As for the game play itself, the UI is great, controls are fast and responsive, I get amazing frame rates and the graphics are surpisingly good considering this is a port to pc from older console era. The voice acting, dialouge, and 90% of the sound effects are really good. A few effects, such as going up and down ladders, leaves a little to be desired. The calls/missions are quite immersive and aren't just a quick point the hose and 3 min later you're back at the firehouse. Good pacing in the action, and the fire behavior is surprisingly good. It becomes a challenge on normal to keep up with larger fires, and the explosions and cave ins are definitely unexpected.
Things I would like to see would be adding a 1920x1080 setting, co-op or multiplayer capability but that's prob a pipe dream.  I would also love to see this game be opened up to workshop mods, a good reshader would do wonders.
All in all, for the price, its worth a buy if you like first person simulation and firefighting games. Good fun time killer thats easy on the wallet and the PC. Definitely recommend it.

Perhaps one of the best F2P games on Steam. Tight controls, feels really nice to play and is very fun.
Gun customisation is awesome and some of the stuff you can make is crazy. Team-healing shotguns. Beam sniper rifles. Cannonball-firing miniguns. Fire elemental laser. Tesla assault rifle. All sorts of crazy crap. Despite the customisation and variety, all gun combinations seem to have been balanced extremely well as there aren't really any weapons that stand out from the rest as being overpowered. They will simply have disadvantages and advantages based on what you've made them into, so just create the guns that suit your playstyle best.
Levelling up in the game can be quite slow at times, taking on a similar levelling pace to Call Of Duty 4/MNC. The in-game currency (Called Blutons) accumulation rate is also quite slow, so unlocking gun parts shouldn't be something done on a whim. Thankfully, the game lets you try before you buy, in an almost seamless (In terms of loading time) shooting range. So you can get a feel for what you're crafting.

I've been playing Loadout for a little bit now and am thoroughly enjoying it. The game supports an Xbox 360 controller with controls similar to Call of Duty, so for me, it was easy to just jump in there and start playing.
I was a little skeptical with the "billions of combinations" that they advertised, so when I started playing I tried to think of what type of weapons I would want. I'm only level 6, but already I have a sniper, (Rifle) and a Shotgun (Pulse) and haven't really felt any imbalance when going against other people. There have been times when a group of 4 players go against me and they completely destroy us, but I think that's partially because they have better coordination.
A few suggestions I have:
1. Make more gun slots accessible without having to pay. For a game that advertises "Billions of Combinations" and has 4 weapons with a VERY wide range of possibility, it seems only natural for you to allow us more options. It's hard to really get into a game when you have to constantly be switching and re customizing your weapon over and over again. The fact that the rifle can be both an assault cannon and a high-powered, bolt-action sniper and ANYTHING in between makes it difficult to be as creative as I can with only 6 permanent possibilities.
2. Make more loadouts accessible without having to pay. 3 Loadouts is nice, but there's still very few possibilities. Take Halo 4 or CoD for instance. In Halo, you gain access to 4(?) loadouts rather quickly, and in Call of Duty, you start out with 5. It's very easy to play in your own way when you have options that are convenient.
3. Make it easier to level up a weapon. Because we're limited in the amount of guns we can make, we have to rely on constantly switching it up. It's difficult to feel progression when you're using each type of weapon with different barrels and scopes and what not, and not making a dent in the experience bar. Even if it requires nerfing each individual level and making more levels overall, it'd be nice to feel like I'm actually progressing with each individual attachment.
4. Increase the base damage of weapons using Pyro ammunition while lowering the burn damage. I understand that the burn damage is "the point" but when a Sniper can kill someone with a headshot, don't you think an incendiary round should do more than a 4th of that? (Headshot hits for 104 with normal round, with Incendiary it hits for 26). It did the rest of the targets health with the burn damage, but it'd be nice for there to be some middle-ground.
5. Increase healing convenience. Healing isn't good enough to really off-set losing that one more heavy-hitter. I'll stick to my class. As a sniper who has a decent idea of what he's doing, my headshots insta-kill (Unless the target has 150% health or a shield) and my body shots hit for 49 damage. It's very difficult for a healer to combat that when they don't even have a bar that shows allies health status. Whether it's a simple UI toggle that shows how much health a teammate has or adding a damage reduction buff as well, I feel that a healing buff would make healing a viable option.
I enjoy the game a lot. I like the customization, the graphics, how people move, the maps, the dance/taunt thing you can do and would recommend this to all my friends, but I think there needs to be a little more for people who aren't paying.
OR you can severely nerf prices, because it costs like, $3 for another loadout, and that adds up pretty quickly.

I like this game, and I would recommend it if you enjoy RTS and space-based games. It's very themeic, endless customisation, and overall a pretty cool game.
One major gripe I have with it is the Warscore system. It's essentially this: you have two 'civs', Civ A versus Civ B. Civ A is a colossal, multiplanetary, robot-driven, hivemind empire. It hates organics, and wants to purge the galaxy. Civ B is a smaller, democracy-based, pacifist empire. Easy game, really.
But in the declaration of war that Civ A has to sign, they have to state the terms of this war. I'm not sure why (aside from game-balance), but this purging, killer robot has to state which planets he wants to take and strip of life. So he does: all of them.
However, that's too much! See, each planet has a certain currency of "warscore" behind it. You can only afford small amounts. So, the killer-genocide machine says "Ok, I'll take...5 planets." he can afford 5.
He does it with ease, and at the end of the war, Civ B accepts surrender, and cedes the planets. Now, it'd be even easier to take Civ B, but the war system has pulled another neat trick: A PEACE TREATY FOR 10 YEARS PRIOR TO THE WAR!
So, while the game lets you create a hivemind, genocide machine, who's mission it is to purge organic life, and can't even hold diplomacy with them, it also tells you that while this machine has no respect for organic life, it does have respect for:
-How many planets they "should" take at a time- wouldn't want to let this end too quickly now, right?
-Peace treaties, because while we are purging their population on other planets, it'd be barbaric to declare war again!
It's a very silly system for war, but also a big system in the game. You can get perks to make things cheaper, but even with all that, it still takes too much warscore for you to Blitzkreig an entire civilization off the galaxy.
7/10- good but the warscore system is quite silly
